descriptionChirho: A burden or load, specifically the heavy labor imposed on the Israelites during their bondage in Egypt, including both the physical loads carried and the system of forced labor itself. All three clusters represent the same noun סִבְלָה with different prepositions and pronominal suffixes ('with/in their burdens,' 'burdens of,' 'to your burdens'). Cross-lingual evidence confirms semantic unity: Arabic أَثْقَال (athqal, heavy loads/burdens), Swahili 'mizigo' (loads/burdens), Hindi बोझ (bojh, burden/load), Korean 짐 (jim, load/burden), Spanish 'cargas' (loads/burdens). All six occurrences relate to the Exodus context (Exod 1:11, 2:11, 5:4-5, 6:6-7).
